clauses.reason: Terminated by its own terms: the order exempts the employee 'until April 30, 1935'. Recorded as 1935-04-30, inclusive (runs through the end of that day) under the owner's 2026-10-21 ruling; the exclusive alternative ends the exemption when that day began. Actor: EO 6106 itself. Later further-exemption orders recorded as later events: EO 7006 (April 10, 1935) recites that Roberts 'was exempted from compulsory retirement for a period of 2 years by Executive Order No. 6106, dated April 10, 1933' and further exempts him until May 1, 1937.

research_rationale:
EO 6106 (April 10, 1933, Franklin D. Roosevelt). Text and identity: read in full in the registered American Presidency Project transcription (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts; grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md (working-text paragraph), done 2026-10-28: the APP page record with the same sha256 in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl has a heading naming EO 6106, its date (April 10, 1933) appears in the held text, and its text_sha256 equals the held file's. Clauses are quoted from that registered file, not from the unregistered clause-drafts copy. It exempts Hugh A. Morrison and David E. Roberts, both of the Library of Congress, who reach retirement age during the current month, from section 204 of the Economy Act of June 30, 1932 until April 30, 1935; both names share the one stated end. Identity: number, date, person and end date agree across the APP page, the census register and the WPA 1944 numbered list. Legal reading: a single time-limited grant that ends by its own terms on 1935-04-30, inclusive. Later orders naming it, recorded as later events with their own dates and quotes: EO 7006 (April 10, 1935) recites that Roberts 'was exempted from compulsory retirement for a period of 2 years by Executive Order No. 6106, dated April 10, 1933' and further exempts him until May 1, 1937. Each recites this order as past history and grants a new period; none revokes or amends this order, so none is this order's end. No later held text names Morrison: the WPA 1944 list summarizes EO 7007 (April 10, 1935) as further exempting 'Hugh A. Morrison, reading room custodian in the Library of Congress' until May 1, 1937, but no text of EO 7007 is held, so it is not recorded as a dated later event; on the WPA summary it would be a separate further exemption, not an end of this order. Searches made on 2026-10-28: (1) census titles in jobs/domesday-register/output/REGISTER.csv with retirement wording for the surname; (2) every WPA 1944 numbered-list entry (jobs/x1-class-engine/data/WPA_NUMBERED_ENTRIES.csv, whitespace-insensitive) for the surname with retirement wording; (3) a full-text search of every held order text under jobs/*/output/texts and jobs/*/data for the person's full name within reach of 'retire' or 'exempt'; (4) a citation search of every held order text for 'Order No. 6106' and list forms ('Orders Nos. ... 6106'). They found, for Roberts, this order and EO 7006; for Morrison, only this order among held texts. Authority: section 204 of Part II of the Legislative Appropriation Act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404), whose proviso lets the President exempt a person from automatic separation at retirement age. No held source shows section 204 repealed or amended before this order's stated end. Held texts of later exemptions show the President still granting exemptions under section 204 through and after this date (EO 7725 of October 12, 1937, running to November 1, 1938, and EO 7842 of March 15, 1938, running to June 1, 1939), which corroborates that the statutory scheme ran through the stated date.
